rationale: 508.4c states a creature put onto the battlefield attacking isn't affected by attack restrictions, so "can only attack alone" is irrelevant; 509.3g states an "attacks and isn't blocked" ability triggers even if the creature was never declared an attacker, e.g. it entered attacking.

609.7a states a player choosing a source of damage may choose any permanent, so a land they control is a legal choice; 614.9 defines the redirection replacement effect that moves the damage to the new recipient.

121.2/121.2a state that draws happen one at a time and that a replacement referring to the number of cards drawn modifies an instruction to draw multiple cards before the individual draws, so it can't apply to a single draw; 504.1 is the one-card turn-based draw-step draw.

121.2 states each of Weave Fate's draws is an individual draw, producing two separate events; 603.2c states an ability triggers once each time its trigger event occurs, so Gitrog triggers twice regardless of how many lands are in each batch.

616.1 states the affected object's controller picks which of the two token replacement effects applies first; 616.1f/614.5 state the process repeats with only still-applicable effects and that an effect gets only one opportunity, so the order doesn't change the result.

903.9b is the commander replacement letting the card go to the command zone instead of the library; 701.24c states the library is still shuffled even though the object was moved elsewhere; 608.2c states the rest of Chaos Warp's instructions are still followed in order.
Two replacement effects apply to the same discard-to-graveyard event; 616.1 (and 616.1e) states the affected object's controller chooses which one to apply, so Nicolas picks the outcome.
608.2c states a spell's controller follows its instructions in the order written, so Smallpox's discard happens before its sacrifice.

509.3c states a "becomes blocked" ability also triggers when an effect causes the creature to become blocked, but only if it was unblocked at that time; 509.1h states the blocked/unblocked state persists until an effect says it becomes blocked.

608.2b states a spell whose only target is illegal doesn't resolve and is put into its owner's graveyard; 109.2 states an unqualified subtype description like "all Sand Warriors" means only permanents on the battlefield, so Crib Swap on the stack isn't exiled.

601.2e is the single legality check, made during proposal while Muldrotha is still on the battlefield; 601.2g states mana abilities are activated after that check and before costs are paid, which is when Muldrotha is sacrificed.

702.37a states morph functions in any zone from which you could play the card, so it works in the graveyard; 702.37c/708.4 state the card is turned face down first and prohibitions apply to those face-down characteristics; 601.3e states those alternative characteristics are what determine whether casting is legal, and a face-down creature card isn't a land.
Both effects are ability-adding/removing, i.e. layer 6 (613.1f); 613.3/613.7 state that within a layer effects apply in timestamp order; 613.8a defines dependency, which the answer rules out here.

702.26a states a phased-out permanent phases in during the untap step of the player under whose control it phased out; 702.26f states continuous effects can expire while it's phased out and no longer affect it when it phases in, so the control effect is gone.
608.2n states an instant is put into its owner's graveyard only as the final part of its resolution, so Beacon Bolt isn't yet in the graveyard when it counts instants and sorceries there.

707.2 states copiable values exclude type-changing and text-changing effects and counters, which is why Lignify's and Figure of Destiny's non-copiable effects aren't conferred; 613.2a/613.1a put the copy effect in layer 1; 613.4b/613.4c place the p/t setting and the Pack's Favor modification in sublayers 7b and 7c.
613.8a defines when one effect depends on another (Conspiracy changes what Dralnu's Crusade applies to); 613.8b states the dependent effect waits and applies afterward.

615.6 states prevented damage never happens, so Angel's Grace has no damage to modify; 615.1a/614.1a distinguish "prevent" (prevention) from "instead" (replacement), which is why Angel's Grace isn't a prevention effect; 615.13/615.5 cover the effect keyed to the amount of damage prevented.

702.85a states cascade compares the exiled card's mana value to the spell's mana value; 118.9c states an alternative cost such as evoke doesn't change the spell's mana cost, and 202.3 derives mana value from that mana cost.
603.3b states abilities that triggered since the last priority are put on the stack by their controller in any order they choose, so the Amulet trigger can be ordered to resolve first.

611.3c states continuous effects from static abilities apply simultaneously with the permanent entering, so Arcbound Ravager is already -1/-1; 704.5f puts a creature with toughness 0 or less into the graveyard; 704.3 states state-based actions are checked before any player gets priority.
603.3d states targets for a triggered ability are chosen as it's put on the stack (following 601.2c-d), so Phantom Beast is targeted before its controller decides anything about resolution.

702.82a defines devour as an as-enters replacement effect placing N +1/+1 counters per creature sacrificed; 614.12/616.1 state that all replacement effects modifying how the permanent enters are checked and applied, so the Paragons' extra counters and devour both apply.
800.4a states that when a player leaves the game, all objects they own leave the game, even ones another player controls.

800.4a covers what happens when Adrien leaves - Highborn Vampire is neither owned nor controlled by him, so nothing happens then; 800.4c states the object is exiled once the control-changing effect ends and its default controller has left the game.

305.3/305.1 state a land can't be played on another player's turn; 305.9 states a permanent that's both land and creature can only be played as a land, not cast, so flash's casting timing never applies; 101.2 gives the "can't" effect precedence, exactly as the answer cites.

614.12 states which characteristics and effects are checked when applying an effect that modifies how a permanent enters - existing continuous effects and already-applied replacements only - so a simultaneously entering Avatar isn't counted.
107.3b states that when a spell with {X} in its mana cost is cast without paying its mana cost, the only legal choice for X is 0.

614.17d states "can't" effects may prohibit a permanent from entering the battlefield; 614.17c states an event that can't happen can only be replaced by a self-replacement effect, so Heart of Yavimaya's as-enters effect never applies.

707.9a states abilities granted as part of a copy effect become part of the copy's copiable values; 707.2 states a copy acquires the original's copiable values, so populating the Heat Shimmer token carries the haste and end-step exile ability.

201.4 states a player choosing a card name must choose a name in the Oracle reference and may not choose a token's name unless it's also a card name; 111.4 states an unnamed token's name is its subtype plus "Token".
704.5q is the state-based action that removes counters, and it names only +1/+1 and -1/-1 counters, so a +0/+2 and a -0/-2 counter coexist.

509.4 states a creature put onto the battlefield blocking is blocking without having been declared as a blocker; 509.4b states it isn't affected by requirements or restrictions that apply to the declaration of blockers.
723.1a states that multiple player-controlling effects on the same player overwrite each other and the last one created is the one that works.

400.6 states replacement effects are applied to a zone change as it happens, so Rest in Peace's effect applies to itself and Fresh Volunteers as they're destroyed simultaneously; 608.2n states Hour of Revelation goes to the graveyard only as the final part of its resolution, after Rest in Peace has left.

606.4 states the cost of a loyalty ability is putting loyalty counters on the permanent; 614.16 states doubling-style replacement effects apply when the effect of a resolving spell or ability, or another replacement effect, places counters, which doesn't cover paying a cost.

613.11 covers continuous effects that modify game rules such as a player's maximum hand size and states they're applied in timestamp order, so Recycle sets it to two and Trusted Advisor then adds two.

702.47c states a spliced spell gains only the rules text of the spliced card and none of its other characteristics, including color; 202.2e states Evermind's color comes from its color indicator, which is therefore not spliced on.

702.15b states damage dealt by a lifelink source causes its controller to gain that much life; 119.9 treats "whenever you gain life" as "whenever a source causes you to gain life," and 702.15e states separate life gain events arise only from multiple sources, so one source damaging four creatures is a single life gain event.

601.2g states mana abilities must be activated before costs are paid; 702.51b states convoke applies only after the total cost is determined and is paid as part of that cost, so Wild Cantor can't both be sacrificed for mana and tapped for convoke.

729.5 states that at the end of a subgame each player puts all traditional cards they own from the subgame into their main-game library and shuffles, explicitly including cards representing phased-out permanents.

614.12a states a choice required by an effect that modifies how a permanent enters is made before it enters, and 400.6 applies replacement effects before the object moves, so both cards are still in the graveyard; 707.5 states an object that enters "as a copy" becomes a copy as it enters.

400.6 states replacement effects apply to the move, so Rest in Peace sends the card to exile instead; 400.7j states other parts of the same effect can find an object it moved to a public zone, so Grenzo still puts it onto the battlefield.
These are the complete set of things protection does - can't be targeted, enchanted, dealt damage, or blocked - and none of them stops a "destroy" effect, which is exactly the answer's reasoning.

616.1 states the affected permanent's controller (Niko) chooses which of the two death-replacement effects applies first; 616.1f states the process then repeats with only still-applicable effects, so the other one does nothing.

616.1 states Ariel chooses which replacement effect to apply to each draw; 702.52a defines dredge as an optional replacement for a draw; 616.1f states the process repeats with the remaining applicable effects, which is why Chains can still apply and be dredged over afterward.

616.1 states Avianna chooses which Chains effect applies first; 614.5 states a replacement effect gets only one opportunity to affect an event or the modified events replacing it, so the first Chains can't apply again to the draw it created.
616.1 states that when two replacement effects would modify the same event, the affected player chooses which to apply, so Adrien picks between Possessed Portal and Tomorrow for the draw-step draw.

616.1 lets Alexis order the applicable enters-with-counters replacements; 614.16 states a "would put one or more counters" effect like Hardened Scales also applies when another replacement effect places the counters; 614.5/616.1f state each effect applies only once, so the total is the same in any order.

616.1a states a self-replacement effect must be chosen first when multiple replacement effects apply, and 614.15 defines self-replacement effects; 616.1f states the process then reconsiders only still-applicable effects, so Blightsteel Colossus's graveyard replacement no longer applies once it's exiled.
